key_insight: CutBackdoor shows that a poisoned VQA parameter set can stay accurate on the full circuit while becoming malicious only when the victim runs circuit cutting, using the cut workflow itself as the backdoor trigger.
engineering_relevance: This exposes a new supply-chain risk for quantum software pipelines that rely on pre-trained VQA parameters and circuit cutting to fit hardware limits.
method: Injects a parameter-level backdoor with no circuit modification.
Uses CutQC-style circuit cutting at deployment time as the activation trigger.
Targets noisy finite-shot cut execution so full-circuit behavior remains stealthy.
evidence_signal: Across IBM backends and multiple VQA benchmarks, the poisoned model increased cut-path energy by about 1.3× to 2.9× over clean baselines while keeping full-circuit stealthiness small.
watch_item: The attack depends on the victim invoking circuit cutting under finite-shot, hardware-constrained conditions, and mitigation such as Zero-Noise Extrapolation only partially reduces the effect.
paper_title: CutBackdoor: A Circuit Cut Triggered Backdoor Attack on Variational Quantum Algorithms
